one_line: A text-first Korean navigation app exposing accessible route and place information to screen readers and agents.
what_it_does: Searches places, returns station accessibility and arrivals, plans routes, and shares the same textual screen state between human screen-reader users and agents.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP consolidates multiple public data sources into precise, shared, screen-reader-compatible route answers and lets the agent move/read the same app state; generic UI driving would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says seven tools chain search, place info, trip planning, route details, and reading the screen.
One tool returns timetable, facilities, elevators, and live arrivals from APIs the agent otherwise cannot call.
Transcript states tools move the app and agent reads what the user does by hand.
execution_rationale: The video transcript directly demonstrates the product rationale, limits, shared screen state, and implementation effort; the app is also reported across web, iOS, CLI, and MCP server.
execution_evidence: 126-second submitted video with transcript.
Transcript reports route answer, 1,500-character limit handling, and screen-reader verification.
About text reports three months of app development, 30 WebMCP commits, and over 100 tests.
impact_rationale: It directly serves blind and screen-reader users with a real accessibility gap in map-centric navigation, including station accessibility details and barrier-free routing.
impact_evidence: Creator identifies lived screen-reader problem and no-map text-first design.
Features include elevators, audio beacons, accessible restrooms, stairs-free routes, and audible crosswalks.
Free, no-account, no-ads availability broadens practical access.
creativity_rationale: Rejecting map-first navigation and making every sentence usable by both screen readers and agents is a distinctive, deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Text-only navigation for South Korea is purpose-built around accessibility.
Route details include which car and door place a user next to an elevator, not merely coordinates.
usability_note: Text-first, screen-reader-compatible output and progressive detail fit the intended users well.
red_flags: Many upstream public/commercial APIs create ongoing data dependency, though this is not a demonstrated defect.
standouts: WebMCP meaningfully improves both agent precision and human-agent shared state.
advance_reason: Top-tier impact, leverage, creativity, and directly evidenced execution for an underserved audience.
